messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

We need to perform t-test on two independent samples. We have dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35] (10 values). Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36] (10 values). We need to compute t-statistic and p-value for alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01. Use two-sample t-test assuming equal variances? Usually independent t-test with equal variances? The problem didn't specify. We'll assume equal variances (pooled). Compute means, variances, pooled variance, t-statistic, degrees of freedom = n1+n2-2 = 18. Then compute two-tailed p-value. Let's compute.

Dataset A: sum = 12+15+18+20+22+25+28+30+32+35 = let's sum: 12+15=27; +18=45; +20=65; +22=87; +25=112; +28=140; +30=170; +32=202; +35=237. Mean_A = 237/10 = 23.7.

Compute sum of squares: For each value, (x - mean)^2. Let's compute quickly.

Dataset B: sum = 14+17+19+21+23+26+29+31+33+36 = let's sum: 14+17=31; +19=50; +21=71; +23=94; +26=120; +29=149; +31=180; +33=213; +36=249. Mean_B = 249/10 = 24.9.

Sum squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22; +34.81=216.03; +15.21=231.24; +3.61=234.85; +1.21=236.06; +16.81=252.87; +37.21=290.08; +65.61=355.69; +123.21=478.90. So variance_B = 478.90/9 = 53.2111. SD_B = sqrt(53.2111)=7.295.

Pooled variance Sp^2 = ((n1-1)*s1^2 + (n2-1)*s2^2)/(n1+n2-2) = (9*57.5667 + 9*53.2111)/18 = (517. + 478.9)/18? Wait compute: 9*57.5667 = 518.1003 (makes sense). 9*53.2111 = 478.8999. Sum = 996.0002. Divide by 18 = 55.3333. So Sp = sqrt(55.3333)=7.435.

Standard error of difference: SE = Sp * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) = 7.435 * sqrt(0.1 + 0.1) = 7.435 * sqrt(0.2) = 7.435 * 0.4472136 = 3.325.

Difference in means: mean_B - mean_A = 24.9 - 23.7 = 1.2.

t-statistic = diff / SE = 1.2 / 3.325 = 0.3608.

Degrees of freedom = 18. Two-tailed p-value: For t=0.361, df=18. Use t distribution. The p-value will be large, >0.7. Let's approximate: t=0.36, df=18, p ~ 0.72? Let's compute using approximate. For df=18, t critical for alpha=0.05 two-tailed is about 2.101. For alpha=0.01, t critical ~ 2.878. Our t is far less. So p-value > 0.7. Let's compute more precisely: Using t distribution table or approximate formula. For df=18, t=0.36, the one-tailed p ~ 0.36? Actually t=0.36 corresponds to p ~ 0.36? Wait t=0.36 is small, so p ~ 0.36? Let's approximate using normal: t=0.36, z=0.36, one-tailed p ~ 0.36? Actually for normal, z=0.36, one-tailed p = 0.359. Two-tailed p = 0.718. So p ~ 0.72. So we can say p > 0.05 and > 0.01. So fail to reject null at both levels.
